items._cn_summary: 本文报道了Colin Currie Group在爱丁堡国际艺术节演出Steve Reich作品的整场音乐会。曲目包括拍手音乐、双钢琴新作、Radio Rewrite、Double Sextet、Quartet以及为三个四重奏和两架钢琴而作的新作In All Your Ways。Currie亲自指挥并参与打击乐演奏，与Owen Gunnell等合作呈现了莱赫极简主义风格中标志性的渐变相位技法与节奏推进。评论详细描述了每首作品的速度变化、结构特点以及在Usher Hall混响空间中的音响效果，对Currie与Reich本人的合作经历也有引用。全文侧重演出实况与作品编排的叙述，文章末尾似乎被截断。

items.album: Death By Love release ‘Królowa Świata’ with Clan Of Xymox bassist Mario Usai
items.excerpt: The bassline on the new Death By Love track was recorded in a hotel room on a North American tour. Królowa Świata, out digitally on 28 August 2026, is the first original song the Polish-American duo have written in Polish, and it carries a guest bass part from Mario Usai of Clan Of Xymox. The gothic, industrial and trip-hop mix Death By Love brought to their debut album “444” is here pushed towards trance-styled synth sequencing. Królowa Świata by Death by Love The release runs four
items.body: The bassline on the new Death By Love track was recorded in a hotel room on a North American tour. Królowa Świata, out digitally on 28 August 2026, is the first original song the Polish-American duo have written in Polish, and it carries a guest bass part from Mario Usai of Clan Of Xymox. The gothic, industrial and trip-hop mix Death By Love brought to their debut album “444” is here pushed towards trance-styled synth sequencing. Królowa Świata by Death by Love The release runs four tracks: “Królowa Świata” (3:44), a “Psychotribe Psychoqueen Remix” of it (3:45), “Forest” (3:53) and a “Psychorchestra Remix” of “Forest” (4:02). Inga Habiba wrote the lyrics and sings; Peter Guellard handled synths and electric guitar; Usai played bass. Guellard produced and mastered the track at his Psychotribe Studio in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The cover picture is by Robert Laska. How Death By Love built ‘Królowa Świata’ on the road The title translates as “Queen of the World”. Habiba addresses the song’s second person to herself rather than to a listener, and describes the writing that way: “these words are the whispers of my own subconscious, trying to break through the defensive armor I had built around myself.” Guellard began work on the track while touring the North American East Coast as a tech for Clan Of Xymox, carrying a portable rig and building around vocal takes Habiba had sent him. He cut the first guitar pass on Ronny Moorings‘ Rickenbacker. Usai then came into his hotel room, listened, and recorded the bass for the whole song. Guellard finished the arrangement at home, pairing fresh vocals from Habiba with the synth sequences. On writing in Polish, he commented: “Poland is our homeland, after all, even though at this point I’ve lived in the US longer than I ever lived there.” The video sets a vampire story in a mansion and a ballroom. Guellard built it from AI-generated imagery that he then edited and reworked with additional visual effects, the same method the duo used on their 2025 video for “Krakowski Spleen”. The track is on Bandcamp, Spotify and YouTube. About Death By Love Death By Love is a Polish-American project built around Polish singer-songwriter Inga Habiba and Polish-born, US-based producer, multi-instrumentalist and remix artist Peter Guellard. Habiba began performing in her teens with the new wave band Nizam, then fronted Monev, Ahimsa and the Warsaw gothic rock group Lorien, and worked with the folk-ethnic ensemble Habiarjan and the electronic act NUN Electro alongside her solo project CallMe. Guellard came up through the Polish goth band Blitzkrieg and later worked in the US dark-electronic underground with MACE, The Electric Hellfire Club, Venus in Furs and Dichro. A remix commission for NUN Electro’s “Hide” led to the pair working together on Habiba’s CallMe material, which became Death By Love. The duo signed to Distortion Productions and opened their catalogue with the three-track single “Strong Inside” at the end of January 2025. A Polish-language cover of Maanam’s “Krakowski Spleen”, with a video assembled from AI-generated visuals, followed in March 2025. They also appeared on COP International’s 75-track wildfire relief compilation “Los Angeles – From The Ashes”. Habiba and Guellard met in Warsaw in October 2024 to record “Strong Inside” and “Temros”, and completed the rest of the album across a year of file exchange between Europe and the United States. The single “Sellenno”, whose video was shot inside the disused Heinz ketchup factory in Pittsburgh, preceded the eleven-track concept album “444”, issued on Distortion Productions on CD and digital in February 2026 with a video for “Cosmic Power”. In July 2026 the duo put out “In Unity” as a set of remixes in tribute to the Polish act Wieloryb. “Królowa Świata” is their first release since.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由波兰裔美籍二人组Death By Love推出的四曲EP，标题曲《Królowa Świata》（世界女王）是他们首支以波兰语创作的作品，邀请Clan Of Xymox的贝斯手Mario Usai在北美巡演期间的酒店房间录制贝斯。制作人Peter Guellard在巡演途中使用便携设备，围绕主唱Inga Habiba的人声素材进行构建，并在Ronny Moorings的Rickenbacker吉他上完成首轮录制。相比首张专辑《444》中哥特、工业与trip-hop的混合风格，此作更倾向于trance式的合成器序列编排。主唱Habiba曾参与多支波兰地下乐队，包括新潮团Nizam、华沙哥特摇滚团体Lorien等，歌词描述潜意识的低语如何突破自我防御。MV采用AI生成图像配合视觉特效呈现吸血鬼与舞厅场景，延续了2025年单曲的影像手法。整体定位介于暗潮工业与舞曲合成器之间，是地下暗潮场景中具有东欧文化背景的合作产物。

items.body: Wrote my Senator, “Senator, what can you do?” But my dear Senator, you sold your soul to AIPAC too. There is something painfully American in the picture Stephen Bluhm draws in Emotional Plea: a man seated before a screen, writing senators, sending money, updating a résumé, scrolling through reports of strangers killed under another sky, while beneath these acts of conscience a disco beat keeps immaculate time. The first single from Work Crush, Bluhm’s quirky new project, takes political despair out of the arena of slogans and places it in the room where most people encounter it, alone with a telephone, a computer, a paycheck, and the knowledge that private life has become entangled with public cruelty. Bluhm, a longtime figure in New York’s Hudson Valley music community, gives that unease an unexpectedly elegant body. Recorded with Alex Wernquest at Basement Floods in Catskill, the song advances on a firm dance rhythm while synthesizers and clipped, Nile Rodgers-like guitar strokes gather around it. Mike Watt, the Minutemen co-founder whose bass playing carries muscle and wit, moves melodically through the track, making the low end feel conversational. Bluhm sings in a cultivated baritone whose theatrical clarity recalls The Magnetic Fields, The Divine Comedy, Joseph Keckler, and Paul Jabara. Aid disappears before reaching those who need it. A senator is accused of surrendering principle to political money. A technology worker recognizes that the product supporting his livelihood may also aid surveillance and imprisonment. Then the view widens toward civilians leaving for work or school beneath falling bombs, and the singer confronts the accident of birthplace separating his safety from their deaths. His question, “what is our dark destiny allowing this to be?” carries the exhausted bewilderment of someone discovering how citizenship, employment, consumption, and conscience can become knotted together. “With Emotional Plea, I’d never written an overtly political protest song, but I felt I couldn’t ignore in my writing what’s happening around us, with ICE, with Gaza, with the complacency and lack of compassion,” says Bluhm. “I usually write slowly, but this came together quickly because I felt it so urgently. Mike Watt is one of the funkiest bass players I know, and I knew he’d be perfect for the song. I’m grateful he agreed. He sent his bass track back within 24 hours. The man works furiously.” The final verse turns toward Christianity, reducing doctrine to an almost childlike attempt at moral imitation. There is humour in the image, though Bluhm sings without a wink; behind it stands an accusation that compassion has become easier to profess than practice. Listen to Emotional Plea below and order the single here. Emotional Plea by Work Crush Work Crush uses no generative AI, and musician-illustrator Steve Teare drew the cover image of a child playing with a toy military plane. It is a severe emblem for a song in which distant violence enters domestic life. After the orchestral intimacy of Bluhm’s Out of the Nowhere Into the Here, this new project finds him facing outward, fastening political dread to bass, beat, and melody, asking how comfortably anyone can dance while the world is simultaneously burning and flooding. What times we live in. Follow Work Crush: Instagram Facebook Website Bandcamp Spotify The post “Senator, What Can You Do?” — New Wave Artist Work Crush Debuts With Political Protest Song “Emotional Plea” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的专辑《The Gods Laugh》以中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心乐器，融合民谣、前卫音乐与宗教冥想气质，形成模糊而神秘的整体氛围。多数曲目为即兴创作并以单次录音完成，部分曲目加入鼓、贝斯与合成器扩展音色层次。评论特别指出《I Am!》以约翰·克莱尔诗作入乐，辅以持续低音铺垫，营造超越感；《Sprigs of Heather》以中世纪圣咏风格开场，发展为钢琴主导的简约级进旋律，被视为专辑核心。专辑也是对 Cotton 已故父亲的纪念之作，丧失与温柔的情绪贯穿始终，尤其在《The Final Harvest》中体现对父亲最后一次前往他所钟爱的小菜园的追忆。明与暗交织，作品拒绝被简单归类，展现出鲜明的个人辨识度。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是一张丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，五首曲目以传统北欧民谣为基础展开。核心是Mia Guldhammer的声线——评论形容其嗓音令人信服且具穿透力。开篇曲以粗粝的奔跑节奏展示人声特质，簧口琴与风笛推动原创曲目前进。匈牙利扬琴为传统叙事曲增添细腻背景层，簧口琴与长笛、弦乐交织的终曲则呈现出略带失调却令人兴奋的器乐张力。整体氛围古老而略带吱嘎感，传统乐器与现代编配意识并存，显示出乐队远超新人水平的成熟度。这张作品是对斯堪的纳维亚民间传统的现代诠释，五轨作为引子已足够有力。

items.album: DELIRIUM Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo (Rock Progressivo Italiano, 2026)
items.excerpt: Review by Stefano61 — Genoa keeps its own kind of light, grey and pressed low over the water, the kind that makes a person feel the years passing even when nothing visible has moved. It was in this city, in 1896, that Eugenio Montale was born, long before he went looking elsewhere for words to describe what that light does to a life. He learned early that the sea does not console. It only continues.Something of that same continuing runs through the other Genoese story this record concerns.
items.body: Review by Stefano61 — Genoa keeps its own kind of light, grey and pressed low over the water, the kind that makes a person feel the years passing even when nothing visible has moved. It was in this city, in 1896, that Eugenio Montale was born, long before he went looking elsewhere for words to describe what that light does to a life. He learned early that the sea does not console. It only continues.Something of that same continuing runs through the other Genoese story this record concerns.In 1970 a covers band called I Sagittari became something else when a young man not yet twenty, Ivano Fossati, joined on flute and voice. Delirium, they called themselves from then on, and within a year they had a hit single, Canto di Osanna, and a debut album, Dolce Acqua, poetic and strange enough that one of its songs lifted a dead man's monologue straight out of Spoon River.Then came Jesahel, sung at Sanremo in February of 1972, the five of them arriving, so the story goes, on a bus borrowed from Genoa's own football club. The song made them, for a season, the most hummed tune in the country.It also, by most honest accounts, did the band more harm than good. Barely a season later Fossati was called away to military service and never really came back, choosing instead a solo path that would make him one of the most respected songwriters Italy has produced, one who quietly left the stage in 2012 and has mostly been writing for others ever since.Even Jesahel would not lie still. Only a few years ago it found itself, entirely without anyone's asking, at the center of an international dispute over whether a much younger American voice had borrowed too freely from its melody, proof that these old Genoese tunes still travel further than 1972 could have guessed.An Englishman, Martin Grice, arrived on flute and saxophone to fill the silence Fossati left, and it was largely through him that the band found the sound of Delirium III, Viaggio negli Arcipelaghi del Tempo, a 1974 record already calling time itself an archipelago to be sailed through. Then, like most things Genoese, the band did not end so much as go quiet, and waited.It surfaces now as Delirium International Progressive Group, with Alessandro Corvaglia singing and adding guitar and keyboards, Michele Cusato on guitar, Fabio Chighini on bass, Enrico Tixi on drums.And there, still, are two threads running straight back to the beginning: Ettore Vigo, at the keyboards since that first 1970 lineup, and Martin Grice, on winds since he first stepped into Fossati's silence in 1972. Fifty four years is a long time to keep walking the same road.Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo, released in May 2026, is in some sense a record about exactly that, about roads and the time that runs alongside them, about how a life, or a band, keeps its shape while everything around it changes.It does not chase anyone's attention. Winds and keyboards still carry most of the weight, as they always have, wrapped now around slower, more patient arrangements and character studies rather than manifestos. The people who populate it are not princes or supermen. They are drifters, the retired, the ones the road passes through rather than the ones who own it, watched with an affection that never curdles into pity.- Schiavo della Vilt�, slave to cowardice, twenty two minutes, nearly an entire vinyl side on its own, and the record's real argument. Cowardice here reads less like a single failing than a paralysis lived quietly for years, and the suite moves through it the way someone moves through an old house at night, recitation giving way without warning to symphonic light, a lyrical passage interrupted before it can settle, tension gathering, releasing, gathering again. It asks of the listener something like the patience Dolce Acqua once asked of a very different generation, back when sitting still with a record was still the ordinary way to spend an evening.- Io Clochard, I am a vagrant, the first human face the record offers once the suite's abstractions have passed, a song that studies a life lived entirely on the pavement with curiosity rather than judgment, the band's old melodic instinct returning gently instead of triumphantly.- Il Riposo del Pirata, the pirate's rest, an old adventurer finally still, the swagger gone out of him along with the urgency, the music settling exactly where its title promises, closer to elegy than to sea shanty.- Della Strada il Ritorno, the road's return, giving something back for once, a shorter piece answering the wandering of what came before with something like arrival, though never quite a homecoming.- Parole nel Vento, words in the wind, the close, scattering rather than gathering, the album ending not on a statement but on something nearer a shrug, which after everything before it feels like the most honest way to stop.Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo does not try to be Dolce Acqua again, and it certainly does not try to repeat the accident of Jesahel. It knows, the way only musicians in their seventies can know, that the years do not grant a second youth, only a longer memory.What it offers instead is the sound of people who never really left the road, telling us, patiently, unhurriedly, what fifty five years of walking it has taught them. Anyone hoping for the old jolt of surprise will have to look elsewhere.Anyone willing to slow to the record's own pace will find a genuinely moving late chapter, faithful to everything the name Delirium has meant, from a bus borrowed for one unforgettable February evening to a Ligurian light that, exactly as Montale found, keeps its secrets simply by continuing. Highly recommended. My rating: 4,5/5

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由意大利老牌乐队Delirum的当代化身完成，延续了乐队自1970年代以来的声音路线。乐评以热那亚的城市气质和诗人蒙塔莱的光线为引子，回溯了乐队从I Sagittari到Delirum的演变，提及Flavio Fossati离队后英国乐手Martin Grice的加入如何塑造了第三张专辑的海上漂流意象。新唱片由Ettore Vigo和Grice两位老成员与新阵容共同呈现，风管与键盘继续承担主干，被包裹在更缓慢、更具冥想感的框架中。整体仍围绕'时间与道路'的母题展开，风格上偏向传统意大利前卫摇滚的抒情与器乐铺陈，未呈现明显的实验或电子跨界。适合对意大利老派前卫摇滚有怀旧情结的听众。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Singularity & Other Stories by Echoes & Signals is another great album from the Russian proggers that shows off great songwriting and technical ability, but it doesn't have the impact of the first album they released this year. While Solar saw the band put forward their strongest material to date, this album is similar in tone but I think it's the short length that brings it down. But having Leo Margarit provide drumming is a massive bonus, as his work with Pain Of Salvation is exceptional and it's just as impressive on this album. With creative use of synths and vocals, overall it still is a great presentation of the band's sound. I'd give this a mid 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Singularity.
items._cn_summary: 俄罗斯乐队Echoes and Signals的第二张专辑延续了前作Solar的氛围基调，在合成器与人声编排上展现出创意，技术功底扎实，鼓手Leo Margarit的加入为作品增色不少。乐评指出专辑整体质量上乘，但在冲击力上略逊于今年发行的首张专辑，篇幅偏短成为主要扣分项。推荐曲目为标题曲Singularity。作为器乐为主、注重结构与氛围的后摇/数学摇滚作品，在技术层面值得肯定，但缺少更极端的实验性突破或跨界融合元素，与纯粹的前卫实验路线尚有距离。

items.body: Chicago post-punk trio French Police released the double single “Super Over Drive” / “Silver” on 28 August 2026 through Interscope Records, with a video for each track. “Super Over Drive” and “Silver” are the band’s second release for the label, four weeks after the “Reptile” / “Japan” double single that opened the deal. Chris Eichenseer directed both clips as a Someoddpilot Studios production and also shot the cover art. The “Super Over Drive” video puts the trio through a sepia-toned performance in which bodies blur into movement and faces appear and disappear. What French Police put on ‘Super Over Drive’ and ‘Silver’ “Super Over Drive” runs 3:22 and rides a driving bass line while Manny Herrera’s guitar cuts back into the arrangement from shifting angles. Brian Flores stretches his phrasing further than on earlier French Police tracks, holding notes past the point where the delivery stays composed. “Silver” runs 3:04, opens the arrangement out and leaves more space around the vocal, trading the first track’s defensiveness for a direct admission. Both tracks are on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and the other streaming services. No album has been announced around them, so they stand as the band’s second standalone Interscope single. The pairing follows “Reptile” / “Japan”, which arrived at the end of July 2026 and was the trio’s first release for a major label after seven years of self-released records and vinyl through independents. Side-Line reported that release in French Police signs to Interscope Records, releases ‘Reptile / Japan’ double single. The Mexican-American singer, songwriter and guitarist writes in Spanish and English. Manny Herrera plays lead guitar and Rolando Donjuan plays bass. The trio bring a post-punk that mixes chorused guitar lines, driving bass and coldwave-leaning vocals, and they share a listener base with Lebanon Hanover, Molchat Doma and The Chameleons. The self-titled debut appeared in 2019, followed by the “Pedaleo Nocturno” EP the same year and the 15-track “Haunted Castle” in February 2020, which Icy Cold Records later pressed to CD. A dense run of self-released EPs and singles followed through 2021 and 2022, among them “Pensamiento Negro”, “Onyx” and “1995”, with “Club De Vampiros / Plant Based Girl” issued by Icy Cold Records in January 2022 and “Fumar / Hate Me” by Cruel Records that May. “Bleu” arrived in February 2023, and Audiotree released a live single and EP the following month. “Bully” came out on 26 January 2024, again self-released digitally with a vinyl edition through Icy Cold Records. Side-Line covered those European pressings in French Police launch limited European vinyl editions of ‘Bully’ and ‘Haunted Castle’, and Side-Line reviewed the album in French Police – Haunted Castle (Album – Icy Cold Records). The “Espera” EP followed in January 2025 with the singles “Sugar Killer” and “Libra” later that year, and Icy Cold Records collected earlier material on the “Essentials” CD in March 2026. The Interscope deal, announced at the end of July 2026, ends the self-released period; “Super Over Drive” and “Silver” are the first songs the band has put out since the tour was announced.
items._cn_summary: 法国警察乐队发行了双单曲《Super Over Drive》和《Silver》，这是他们与Interscope厂牌合作的第二支单曲。《Super Over Drive》以紧凑的贝斯线驱动，吉他从多角度切入，人声在极限处拉伸超出惯常的克制表达。《Silver》则展开了更宽松的编曲空间，人声周围留白更多，从前者的防御性转向直接的坦露。视频由Chris Eichenseer执导，采用棕褐色调，画面中人物轮廓模糊、面容闪现隐没。七年的独立厂牌生涯后，这支芝加哥后朋克三人组通过两支双单曲系列进入主流厂牌体系，目前尚无专辑计划，仍以独立单曲形式发行。整体延续了后朋克与暗潮的语汇，在结构与情绪上呈现成熟稳定的处理，但未见明显的实验性突破。

items.body: Italian darkwave and post-punk trio Soft Scent release “No Flowers in June” on 21 September 2026, together with an official music video. It is the first single from “Mother’s Ruin”, the band’s second album and the follow-up to their 2024 debut “CHIMERA”. Pre-orders for a physical edition open on Bandcamp on 29 August 2026. That physical edition runs to fifty individually numbered CDs, self-released by the band. Each copy ships in a black envelope sealed with one of six flower wax seal designs, picked at random per copy, and comes with a printed art card carrying the artwork and credits. Who recorded ‘No Flowers in June’ Gianluca Lo Presti recorded the track at Loto Studio 2.0 in Filetto and at Logan Sound Space in Castelfidardo, Italy. Lo Presti also recorded Soft Scent’s debut album at the earlier Loto Studio. William Faith, a founding member of Faith and the Muse, mixed and mastered it at 13 Studio in Los Angeles. The song keeps the band’s darkwave and post-punk footing, with a restless bassline and insistent synthesizers. “Mother’s Ruin” is built as a concept album in the form of a travel book, moving between places, eras and stories. The title takes the Victorian nickname for gin, and the band set the record between comfort and destruction, escape and consequence. “No Flowers in June” deals with what is left once the escape is over. Soft Scent describe the song in one line: “Some endings don’t wait, they arrive before you do.” The artwork follows the album’s visual language, using dried and ceramic flowers marked with eyes modelled on Victorian Lover’s Eyes miniatures. No release date has been announced for “Mother’s Ruin”. About Soft Scent Soft Scent formed in Marche, Italy, in the summer of 2023, as a trio: Anna, who performs as MissLucifer, on vocals, keyboards and synthesizers; Enrico on drums and electronic drums; and Sara on bass and backing vocals. The band write and produce their own material. Their first single, “The Howl”, appeared in November 2023, followed by “No Wounds” in January 2024 and the title track “Chimera” that August. The debut album “CHIMERA” came out on 9 September 2024, running seven tracks: “Parasomnia”, “No Wounds (Album Mix)”, “Chimera”, “17:07”, a cover of Grauzone‘s “Wütendes Glas”, “The Howl (Album mix)” and “Susan and Sam”. Gianluca Lo Presti recorded it at Loto Studio in Filetto, and Maurizio “Icio” Baggio mixed and mastered it at La Distilleria Studios in Sarcedo. Tommaso Pompili added backing vocals and guitar to “The Howl”. The Polish label Bat-Cave Productions issued the CD in a six-panel digipack with a lyrics poster insert, and Manic Depression Records handled the vinyl. CHIMERA by Soft Scent Two remixes of the album tracks followed, by Ermete Lo Stige and Border. “No Flowers in June” is the band’s first new recording since, and the first material from the second album.

items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于Miles Davis与John Coltrane合作时期所用贝斯手的编年史式梳理。以Paul Chambers为核心，从《Kind of Blue》与《Giant Steps》两张经典专辑切入，追溯Chambers在底特律Cass Technical High School的成长背景、1954年赴纽约后的录音生涯，以及他与Davis长达数年的合作关系。文章详述了Chambers在1959至1963年间参与的百余次录音，包括Benny Golson、Wynton Kelly等爵士音乐家的专辑，随后转向对其离世后Davis乐队贝斯手更替的探讨。作为学术性爵士乐评，文章注重史实考据与乐手谱系，文字扎实但偏向传记式叙述，缺乏对音乐本体声响或即兴语汇的深度分析。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body: The Cure released their sixth studio album, “The Head on the Door,” on 30 August 1985 through Fiction Records. The album turns 41 this year. It followed 1984’s “The Top” and arrived with a lineup that added drummer Boris Williams and brought back bassist Simon Gallup and guitarist Porl Thompson. The band recorded “The Head on the Door” in 1985 at Angel Recording Studios in London. Robert Smith and David M. Allen produced the album, with Howard Gray producing “Kyoto Song,” “Push” and “A Night Like This,” and Frank Barretta engineering. The ten-track record runs “In Between Days,” “Kyoto Song,” “The Blood,” “Six Different Ways,” “Push,” “The Baby Screams,” “Close to Me,” “A Night Like This,” “Screw” and “Sinking.” It was issued on vinyl LP and CD, led by the single “In Between Days,” which reached number 15 on the UK Singles Chart, and followed by second single “Close to Me.” “The Head on the Door” reached number seven on the UK Albums Chart and number 59 in the US, and is certified gold in the US, UK and France. It streams on Spotify. About The Cure The Cure formed in Crawley, England, in 1976, when school friends Robert Smith and Lol Tolhurst played together in a band that became Malice, then Easy Cure. Easy Cure signed briefly to the German label Ariola-Hansa in 1977, but the deal collapsed in 1978 after the label rejected the song “Killing an Arab” and pushed for cover versions instead. Guitarist Porl Thompson was dropped from the lineup in April 1978, and Smith renamed the remaining trio the Cure. Later that year, Polydor scout Chris Parry signed the band to his newly formed Fiction label. The Cure released the single “Killing an Arab” in December 1978 and its debut album, “Three Imaginary Boys,” in May 1979. Bassist Simon Gallup joined for “Seventeen Seconds” (1980), an album that helped shape the emerging gothic rock sound, followed by “Faith” (1981) and “Pornography” (1982). Gallup left after the “Pornography” tour, and Smith put the Cure on hold to join Siouxsie and the Banshees as guitarist. Tolhurst switched from drums to keyboards, and the pair released the singles “Let’s Go to Bed” (1982), “The Walk” and “The Love Cats” (1983), later compiled on “Japanese Whispers.” For 1984’s “The Top,” Smith played most of the instruments himself, drummer Andy Anderson and early Malice member Porl Thompson filled out the sessions, and Thompson officially rejoined the band. During the following tour, Boris Williams, previously the touring drummer for Thompson Twins, became the Cure’s official drummer, and Gallup rejoined after reconciling with Smith. This lineup of Smith, Tolhurst, Gallup, Williams and Thompson recorded “The Head on the Door” in 1985, and the album’s success carried into the “Standing on a Beach” singles compilation the following year. The Cure went on to release “Kiss Me, Kiss Me, Kiss Me” (1987), “Disintegration” (1989) and “Wish” (1992), and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019. The band’s most recent studio album, “Songs of a Lost World,” arrived in November 2024 after a 16-year gap, followed by the remix collection “Mixes of a Lost World” in June 2025. The Cure returned to Rockfield Studios in March 2025 to record 13 songs for a follow-up album, placing “The Head on the Door” anniversary within an active chapter of the band’s ongoing work.

Allen的制作分工。作为暗潮与后朋克领域的经典专辑，《The Head on the Door》在风格上属于新摇摆时期的The Cure，融合了流行敏锐度与哥特阴郁底色，单曲《In Between Days》和《Close to Me》具有较强的传播力。整篇内容为信息性纪念稿，缺乏对音乐语言、制作美学或历史意义的深度评论。

items.body: Nine Inch Nails released “Hesitation Marks” on 30 August 2013 through The Null Corporation, distributed by Columbia Records in the United States and Polydor Records elsewhere. The eighth studio album by Trent Reznor‘s industrial rock project turns 13 this year. It was the band’s first full-length release in five years, following 2008’s “The Slip,” and its only album distributed through Columbia. “Hesitation Marks” was produced by Reznor alongside Atticus Ross and Alan Moulder, Reznor’s longtime studio collaborators; it remains the most recent Nine Inch Nails album to be co-produced by Moulder. The standard edition runs 14 tracks: “The Eater of Dreams,” “Copy of a,” “Came Back Haunted,” “Find My Way,” “All Time Low,” “Disappointed,” “Everything,” “Satellite,” “Various Methods of Escape,” “Running,” “I Would for You,” “In Two,” “While I’m Still Here” and “Black Noise.” Guest musicians on the record include Lindsey Buckingham, Adrian Belew, Pino Palladino and Ilan Rubin. Tom Baker handled mastering. Cover art across the album’s several editions was created by Russell Mills, the artist behind the visuals for “The Downward Spiral” nineteen years earlier. Three singles preceded the album: “Came Back Haunted” (June 6, 2013), “Copy of a” (August 13, 2013) and “Everything” (August 20, 2013). “Hesitation Marks” debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 and topped the Canadian Albums Chart, and was nominated for the Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Album at the 56th Annual Grammy Awards. About Nine Inch Nails Nine Inch Nails was formed by Trent Reznor in 1988 in Cleveland, Ohio. Reznor wrote, arranged and performed nearly all instrumentation on the band’s debut album, “Pretty Hate Machine,” released via TVT Records in 1989. After a dispute with TVT over promotion, Reznor signed with Interscope Records and released the EP “Broken” in 1992, followed by “The Downward Spiral” (1994) and “The Fragile” (1999). Nine Inch Nails returned from a hiatus with “With Teeth” (2005) and “Year Zero” (2007), then left Interscope and independently released the instrumental double album “Ghosts I-IV” and “The Slip,” both in 2008, before entering a second hiatus. Reznor announced the return of Nine Inch Nails in February 2013 and confirmed on May 28, 2013 that a new album, recorded in secret with Atticus Ross and Alan Moulder, was finished. That record, “Hesitation Marks,” followed on August 30, 2013, backed by the Twenty Thirteen Tour featuring Reznor, Ross, Robin Finck, Alessandro Cortini, Josh Eustis and Ilan Rubin. Ross, previously a production collaborator, became an official member of Nine Inch Nails in 2016. Subsequent releases include the EPs “Not the Actual Events” (2016) and “Add Violence” (2017), the album “Bad Witch” (2018), and “Ghosts V: Together” and “Ghosts VI: Locusts,” both released in 2020. Nine Inch Nails was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2020. “Hesitation Marks”, the album that ended the band’s second hiatus, turns 13 this year.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是对Nine Inch Nails第八张录音室专辑《Hesitation Marks》发行十三周年的纪念性回顾，主要以事实陈述为主，涵盖了专辑的发行信息、厂牌背景、制作团队、客座乐手、曲目列表及商业成绩。文章追溯了Trent Reznor自1988年组建乐队以来的厂牌变迁历程，并提及该专辑在公告牌排行榜上的表现及格莱美提名。文章本质上是新闻性质的回顾稿，缺乏对专辑音乐本身的深度分析或批评性评价，未涉及制作手法、声音设计或艺术成就的探讨。对于关注工业、暗潮及电子音乐的读者而言，文章提供的音乐评论价值有限，信息以背景资料为主。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Nine years after their underwhelming 2025 'Beast, Machine & Man', this Finnish combo returns with 'Monologue of Chronos' with the home of reigniting the rave reviews for their 2006 debut 'Armed Forces of Simantipak' as well as the follow-up 'Disconcerto Grosso' , both most enjoyable recordings . Essentially now a trio of Atte Kurri, Ilkka Piispala and Ilkka Saarikivi, all pretty much multi-instrumentalists, as well as participating in the vocal department, this is quite the tight package containing seven mid-sized tracks. A wide variety of keyboards usurp the stage, the main motor in composing and creating the appropriate sonic groundwork, while the rhythm section remains lively within the process. The end result is perhaps closer to more progressive versions of 10cc or even Supertramp, pretty overt in the vocal harmonies that made the two bands in questions such powerhouses. Thrown in burly bass guitar settings, and pumping piano, organ and synthesizer motifs with impunity and you get the picture. One immediate observation is that the harmonies clearly outshine the lead vocals, which can be a tad reedy and thin at times, it's an oddity that does not condemn the arrangements in any manner. As befits a monologue I guess, there are no uneven tracks here, as all seven form a setlist with enough diversity and instrumental technique that have both Neo and Symphonic characteristics. On occasion, the screeching guitar leaps out and bites, on others it's the obdurate bass lines that provide the thrills, a modern approach that eschews any need for senselessly flashing solos, preferring amore cohesive overall experience. After the first two tracks set the standard and the pace, the album really starts hitting its groove on the relentless 'The Dystopian Spirit of Club Energy', the instrumental core attracting quite a few raised contented eyebrows. This impression blooms even further on the impressive 'Song of Days', a pummelling onslaught that delivers the goods, a poignant drum beat in particular doing a fair amount of damage, as if urging the symphonics to take over, while shifting the urgency at will, keeping the drama intense. The cute Yes-isms are both adorable and reverential, the slippery axe solo a total blast and the percussion throughout subtle and a propos. These two tracks easily outduel the aging affirmative crew as well as those Asia guys. Me like this. 'DID Memoir' introduces a gorgeous piano within a melody to die for, bold and adventurous, as the development takes the tempo into a comfort zone, a prog power ballad! The keyboards have an echoing tone that is most modern and utterly appealing. On a dime, the switch is momentarily flipped and a jazzier mood hits one right between the ears! Another button is pressed and the rush returns like a long-withheld memory. A semi-rap section had me fall off my chair, a clever little insert that clicked on all cylinders. The intertwined vocal harmonics come back for an encore on 'The Keepers of Philosopher's Stone', the piano and bass playing together, as if building sandcastles on the beach, the assorted keyboardists doing a few Gentle Giant stylistics to confuse the audience. There is an ongoing battle between complex arrangements, loaded with experimentation, such as the harpsichord patch, veering into an organ splurge that would make Kerry Minnear smile and a sense of accessibility that dares not to give way to familiarity.Well appointed theatrics appear on the finale 'Mundus Meus (This World of Mine)', so as it leave a positive last impression. It's also the longest track by a few seconds, with a stunning chorus and a series of wicked guitar abrades, a fitting example of nailing the deal. The neo-Gregorian choir bit really hit the spot. An entertaining modern prog album that deserves a commitment to listen with an open mind, and enjoy all of its constructive attributes. A few spins will get it done. 4 Armenian speeches

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Milanese quintet releases their third album, following their 2017 debut "Alight" and "Nautilus" which came two years later, both well received. The band continues to feature vocalist Francesco Lovari (whose English is as great as his lung capacity) , Alessandro Palmisano handling all matters guitar, Niccol� Gallani shuffling his keyboard arsenal while the family tandem of Loris Bersan on bass duties and Eric Bersan doing the drums and percussion chores. Nine years and no line-up changes, lovely move! "Wasted Potential" is a clever opening title that has zero bearing on the music proposed here, introducing the blustering keys, the thrilling voice, the rhythmic duo in full force and a shrugging guitar shroud, with less than 5 minutes, preciously condensed and intense. This is moder RPI, firmly ensconced in the schizoid 21st century, freshly brash and slash. A tremendous sizzler. Following that slap in the face with a sense of humour-laden "Please Be Gentle" is a proof positive that no one does drama better than our Italian Fratelli! Once again, the savvy interplay shows a team spirit that can only be admired (since the 'squadra' sucks lately, this is all one can have!), Gallani's moaning mellotron forging massive choral swoops, the bass and guitar smashing harshly and the percussive thuds very remote from tender facility. 2 shots, 2 goals, time for an epic! The 11 and a half minute long "The Case of the Silent Queen" evokes pastoral emanations of acoustic splendour (early Genesis and Anthony Phillips), the delicate arrangement increasing in intensity at a 'gentle' pace, the exuberant piano and drum cooperation making this a most flavoursome affair, the symphonics kicking in with romantic glee, as the mellotron keeps on glowing. The transitional variations are subtle, keeping the emotional impact well entrenched between the ears, dabbling bits of choir and thrashing cymbals awakening the soul. Suddenly, the not-too silent explosion arrives, led by an obsessive synthesizer loop, hushed vocal effects, and occasional axe-driven slashes that thunder without remorse. With all cylinders revving mightily, the lister's pulse cannot help racing forward into another realm of consciousness, no hint of filler or dross, just straight on musical theater for the demanding prog fan. Absolute master class demonstration. A little well-deserved respite is called for, after such a harrowing experience. "We Need to Talk" is exactly that, an effortless human grievance, we all have endured too many times. Heartbreak, heartache, loss, separation, distance, fate, called it what you will. The lyrics take their warranted place , upfront and center, as if "it was meant to be". A stunning vocal chorale, Palmisano shining on acoustic, Gallani burning on his keys, the Bersans keeping it all tightly wrapped in bliss. "Caged" is the other longer track, and as the title suggests , it's a heavily claustrophobic musical enclosure, the hyper piano possessed throughout, Lovari singing like an incarcerated victim of circumstance, no access to a phone or a ticket to freedom. We are stuck in limbo, and all alone. The screeching guitar solo secretes the angst for the longing of escape, the bass desperately searching for a way to open the locks, leading to the outside. When those damned mellotrons blow the roof off the penitentiary , the raging guitars in full collusion, the deed is done. Free at last. Maintaining the focus on the human condition, "The Day We Never Met" offers a jazzier vibe, weighed down by brooding e-piano and synth evolutions, a lovely contrast between melody and dissonance, but within a completely different style compared to the rest of the album. You may have guessed by now, and yes, the sturdy mellotron once again blows into the midst with thunderous resilience. Extraordinarily seductive. The title track puts this exceptional album to rest, a well-deserved siesta after a completely entertaining performance. As a fitting finale, the piece sort of encompasses the underlying thrill of the entire album, strengthening the beliefs in the talent presented here. Its everything one may want from modern day progressive rock. Please continue, and never get out of you strident grotto. 4.5 Anxious fibs

items.body: Review by alainPP — 1. "The Storm" captures a mood of melancholy?oozing guitar tones followed by percussive pounding and Riccardo's vintage keyboards launching the final solo. The lead guitar work is meltingly smooth and delicate?a real treat.2. "Sandsend" follows, with guitar supported by keyboards once again?Steve's guitar (the veteran member, if I'm not mistaken). It's a sweet, ambient, dreamy melody that casts a spell without overcomplicating things. Daniele's keyboard and percussion work is worth noting here.3. "Red Dragon" appeals immediately with its Celtic opening featuring bagpipes. I don't see a red dragon on the horizon, but rather a tune oscillating between Ireland, Scotland, and the Maghreb?a delicate blend of sounds that unite different worlds, which is what matters most. The guitars feel airy, plaintive, and hopeful, drifting into a dreamlike state. It features a radiant horn outro.4. "The Roaring Waves" arrives; if that isn't Steve playing, then it certainly sounds like him?delivering a magnificent, warm arpeggio over a chord progression reminiscent of classic Genesis (see if you can spot the influence). Those crystalline notes, plucked one by one, evoke an illustrious past. The track builds into a breathtaking solo?simple yet intense. The mood turns solemn, like a funeral march, with guitars?both acoustic and electric?softening before leading the listener into a neo-classical melodic passage; a gentle finale.5. "K-129" has a Gabriel-esque vibe?reminiscent of his world music work, specifically the *Birdy* soundtrack?creating an immersive, tribal atmosphere. There's a touch of 80s-era Genesis synth?or even Tangerine Dream?in that repetitive keyboard line. Daniele's dark percussion kicks off the guitar's wandering melody, building into a mantra-like crescendo. The track wouldn't be complete without that heart-wrenching solo?classic-era Marillion style: simple yet flawless.6. "The Black Sea" sees Leon on percussion?specifically a Hang drum with a touch of vintage vinyl crackle. The guitar tone is Floyd-esque and atmospheric, offering an enchanting, cinematic bluesy melody that feels like the perfect soundtrack for a TV series. Steve launches into a melancholic solo over a rising build-up?yet another one?that elevates the emotion to heavenly heights. It ends with a decrescendo accompanied by crackling sounds.7. "Pacific Coast Highway" marks a radical shift in sound; the American West comes alive with a festive, Western-rock vibe?think Chet Atkins?that makes you want to dance energetically and forget your age. Steve Hackett has a blast on the harmonica?at least you know it's him?while Riccardo treats us to an organ solo that harks back to the instrument's glory days. I detect a hint of Dire Straits in the fiery guitar work; my legs start moving and breaking into a dance. Halfway through, the acoustic guitar takes on a growly, Supertramp-esque edge before shifting into a linear guitar solo?not technical, just brimming with feeling and resonance. The finale is Oldfield-esque and pastoral, featuring a sensual, bucolic choir and a flute appearing out of nowhere to close the track.(3.5)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Steve Hackett与Rothery的合作项目，横跨前卫摇滚、凯尔特世界音乐与新古典主义等多个领域。整体以吉他为主导，融入风笛、手鼓等传统乐器，尝试将欧洲民谣、北非马格里布旋律与Genesis式经典前摇语汇进行融合。多首作品带有冥想式渐进结构与电影配乐般的氛围铺陈，但在声效设计上偏向怀旧与抒情，少有突破性的实验元素。专辑标题虽以Eclectic Prog（折衷前卫）自居，但实际呈现更接近复古摇滚与新古典吉他独奏的结合，跨界融合停留在表面层次。

items.body: Review by Prog Dog — On my way over to finally dig into Neal Morse's album for my first review, I stumbled across an email I'd overlooked about his brother Alan's recent solo album. My curiosity got the better of me, and I was not disappointed. In fact, I feel like I've made a new guitar friend. Alan is a serious axe player and a very good songwriter to boot, and I've been quite taken by his soulful style and technique throughout this tastefully produced disc. This also proves the lyric from his title track, "Everyday Is Insane." Not really, but thank goodness for spontaneity.This is his second solo album (I haven't yet heard the first), and it's an impressive showcase of the man's very creative and understated solo work. There's very little repetitiveness or redundancy across this collection of eleven tunes, testifying to the abundance of raw source material he is drawing on here. If you're not fond of a song or a moment in a song, just wait a a minute and something completely fresh will come up next. After a few listens I find that I might not be in the mood for a track or two but I generally enjoy it all. He calls on a long list of friends and family to help out on various instruments and background vocals, and there's probably no shortage of familiar names here, least of all his brother Neal (by the way is Neal the big brother? or the little brother??). Tony Levin's presence caught my eye right away. And daughter Julia sings on "Making Up My Heart," which strikes me as a really sweet and personal touch, and a lovely reminder that the line of musical talent runs deep through the Morse family.This is essential listening for any serious Spock's Beard fan, of course, since that's Alan's main gig, and most of the band helps out.To me, though, this is a guitarist's album. Oh, wait, it's a real treat for drummers as well. The drum kits sound amazing and sit tight and loud in the mix throughout, and there's this ripper of a solo at the end of "Making Up My Heart". On the drum throne are some notable players: Simon Phillips, Jimmy Keegan, John Morse and, of course, Nick D'Virgilio.Alan isn't really lead-singer material in the sense of fronting a top-tier band on the world stage, but in a personable singer-songwriter setting, he's more than pleasant company for the ears.Since Alan is proficient in almost any stringed instrument, and he plays more than just guitar on the album. Not sure exactly how many but I heard bouzouki, cello, mandolin, and electric sitar. Not the most attractive album cover, but once you hear what's under the hood, you'll warm right up to it. There are almost party-rock vibes to some of the album, think Van Halen or that unmistakable '80s energy. I hear hints of classic Saga and perhaps '80s Rush as well. It's a thoroughly enjoyable listen for a guitarist and prog fan like me.Prog Dog score: 3.5 out of 5 &/or 3 out of 5 for the progarchives system.
items._cn_summary: Alan Morse的专辑展现了一位多乐器吉他手的精湛技艺，融合了爵士摇滚、前卫摇滚元素，偶有Van Halen式的八十年代派对能量和Rush式的气息。制作精良，邀请了多位知名乐手参与，包括鼓手Nick D'Virgilio、Simon Phillips、贝斯手Tony Levin等，吉他音色soulful且技术扎实。女儿Julia的客串演唱增添了家庭温度。作为Spock's Beard成员的个人solo作品，延续了乐队基因但更偏向吉他手展示和创作型歌手的氛围。评论者给出3.5/5分，认为是吉他爱好者与前卫乐迷的悦耳之选，但对追求实验性、先锋性或极端融合的听众而言，风格仍偏传统主流融合框架内，缺乏突破性的声音设计或跨界探索。
